Posterior summaries under several priors

Source: R/compare.R
prior_sensitivity.Rd

Refits a posterior under each of several priors on the between-site standard deviation and collects the fits in a comparison, to see how much the diagnostics depend on the prior.

Usage

prior_sensitivity(x, priors)

Arguments

x

An object of class reliability_posterior.

priors

A named list of priors made by sd_prior().

Value

An object of class profile_comparison whose first analysis is x itself, named after its prior.

Details

With few sites the flat prior on the standard deviation can matter (Gelman, 2006): its posterior has a heavy upper tail. A half-normal or half-t prior whose scale is set on the scale of the effects is a common alternative. The comparison shows how far the conclusions move; it does not choose a prior. The scale of a proper prior has no default, because it depends on the units of the estimates.

References

Gelman, A. (2006). Prior distributions for variance parameters in hierarchical models (comment on article by Browne and Draper). Bayesian Analysis, 1(3), 515-534. doi:10.1214/06-BA117A

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, data = eight_schools)
prior_sensitivity(fit, list(
  `half-normal, scale 10` = sd_prior("half_normal", scale = 10),
  `half-t, scale 10, 3 df` = sd_prior("half_t", scale = 10, df = 3)
))
#> Comparison of 3 analyses
#> Intervals are central posterior intervals.
#> Each analysis is conditional on its own standard errors.
#> 
#>   analysis                J  informativeness I     mean reliability
#>   flat                    8  0.225 [0.000, 0.745]  0.230
#>   half-normal, scale 10   8  0.157 [0.000, 0.570]  0.162
#>   half-t, scale 10, 3 df  8  0.156 [0.000, 0.587]  0.161
#> 
#>   analysis                dispersion H             concentration count J_eff
#>   flat                    0.0143 [0.0000, 0.0283]  7.2
#>   half-normal, scale 10   0.0118 [0.0000, 0.0282]  7.1
#>   half-t, scale 10, 3 df  0.0116 [0.0000, 0.0282]  7.1
